newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL rubber extends gains at close, trade slow.
newsitem.headline: KL rubber extends gains at close, trade slow.

text.p: The Malaysian rubber market extended gains at the close due to rallies in the Tokyo market, but trading was cautious with players concerned about further developments on Thailand's move to default on a rubber deal, dealers said.
"Basically the market is cautious. One thing is because of Thailand's decision to default on a rubber deal...and the other one is about the currency factor," a dealer said.

"The market is confused. People are still assesing the Thailand news," he said, expecting that prices would fall as Thailand may have more rubber to sell, whether it's for nearby or forward shipments.
Thailand Deputy Prime Minister Sukhawich Rangsitphol announced on Thursday that Bangkok will not take delivery of the rubber to trim losses on an official scheme to prop up domestic rubber prices.
On the demand side, there was no interest from Europe due to the summer holiday while Far East consumers saw little interest on SMR 10 and SMR 20 for prompt shipment, dealers said.
A fall in the ringgit against the U.S. dollar continued to underpin the market which was influenced by the Thailand default news, dealers added.
